subject: Q3 usage reconciliation & settlement proposal
messages:
From: Emma Chen <emma@nimbus.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Sam Torres <sam@nimbus.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbus.ai
Date: Sat, 01 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Q3 retro usage — reconciliation request

Hi Vivek —

We ran our Q3 billing reconciliation and flagged a material amount of retroactive usage that wasn’t covered by our committed capacity for July–Sep. I’ve attached a CSV that breaks the calls and tokens by day (nimbus_q3_usage_report.csv). The total overage comes to $42,300.

Can Redwood issue a one-time invoice for the overage or advise if there’s an alternative (account credit, prepaid true-up)? We need this cleaned up before we finalize our Q4 forecast.

HubSpot deal: HUB-5582 (committed plan renewal in discussion).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

—Emma
Emma Chen
Head of Cloud Ops, Nimbus Analytics
emma@nimbus.ai

Attachments:
- nimbus_q3_usage_report.csv (CSV, 124 KB)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 14:05:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: Q3 retro usage — reconciliation request (internal)

Looping you in — Nimbus sent the attached usage file and is asking for a one-time invoice of $42.3k. Quick thoughts:

- We rarely bill full list for retro usage when there was a visible spike that could be correlated to onboarding or an integration bug.
- Suggest we propose a blended settlement: 80% cash invoice + 20% account credit (helps preserve relationship and nudges toward committed expansion).
- If finance okays, we should offer a short addendum to increase committed capacity starting Jan 1 to avoid repeats. That can be tied to a 12-month renewal discount.

Marissa — can you run the numbers and draft an invoice? Neha — can you confirm billing treatment and whether we can apply a credit line item? Sean — any commercial objections?

Thanks,
Vivek
CEO (mailbox) — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 10:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q3 retro usage — reconciliation request (internal)

Thanks — I ran the numbers off Emma's CSV. If we accept 80% of their requested amount the cash invoice would be $33,840. I’ve attached a draft one-time invoice (redwood_one_time_invoice_202511_draft.pdf) with breakdowns: base overage, pro-rated reserved discounts, and a line for a 20% account credit to be issued on settlement.

Notes:
- I applied the standard reserved discount where usage maps to periods that were clearly outside committed capacity (per our meter logs).
- If we mark the credit as a one-off promotional credit tied to the renewal, finance will prefer a memo that it’s non-refundable and expires in 9 months.

Next steps: confirm accounting treatment, confirm numbers with Emma, prepare final invoice + DocuSign addendum to expand committed capacity (target effective date 2026-01-01).

Attachments:
- redwood_one_time_invoice_202511_draft.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

—Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q3 retro usage — reconciliation request (internal)

I like the blended approach but propose a slight tweak to improve stickiness: 60% cash + 20% credit + 20% applied as an early-payment discount on their renewal commitment. Example math on $42.3k:
- Cash invoice (60%): $25,380
- Account credit (20%): $8,460
- Renewal early-pay discount value (20%): we bake into the renewal ARR uplift and reflect as a one-time deduction when renewing.

Reason: preserves revenue recognition now while giving Nimbus immediate operational relief and a tangible renewal benefit. Helps us land the upsell to a higher committed tier.

If everyone agrees, Marissa can draft two artifacts: final invoice and a short addendum that increases the committed capacity by X GPUs / token volume starting 2026-01-01.

—Sean
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Torres <sam@nimbus.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Emma Chen <emma@nimbus.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 16:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Q3 retro usage — reconciliation request

Vivek / Emma — thanks for the quick internal review. Nimbus is willing to accept the blended settlement Sean proposed:
- Cash payment: $25,380 (one-time invoice)
- Account credit: $8,460 applied within 30 days
- We agree to sign a short addendum to raise our committed capacity starting 2026-01-01; procurement will route the DocuSign.

Can you send the final invoice and the addendum for signature? Procurement copied here (procurement@nimbus.ai).

—Sam
Account Executive, Nimbus Analytics
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam@nimbus.ai>, Emma Chen <emma@nimbus.ai>, procurement@nimbus.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 11:12:00 -0000
Subject: Final settlement and next steps — Nimbus Q3 true-up

Thanks, all — glad we could reach a speedy resolution. Per the thread above, Redwood will proceed as follows:

1) Final invoice: $25,380 (one-time charge) attached as redwood_final_invoice_202511.pdf. Payment terms: Net 30.
2) Account credit: $8,460 to be issued to Nimbus’s account within 30 days of payment. Credit will expire 9 months from issue and is non-refundable.
3) Addendum: DocuSign link for the committed-capacity addendum is below; effective date 2026-01-01. Please have procurement sign by 2025-11-20 to ensure setup lead time.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/share/ABC123-redwood-nimbus-addendum
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HUB-5582

Marissa / Neha — Marissa will upload the final invoice to our finance system and Neha will confirm accounting entries. Marissa — please dispatch the PDF and the DocuSign envelope.

Sam/Emma — once signed we’ll schedule a short onboarding session for the expanded capacity and share recommended batching/quantization settings to limit future spikes.

Thanks,
Vivek
CEO — Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_final_invoice_202511.pdf (PDF, 54 KB)
